title: Nuclear membrane-tethered FRAP method for measuring protein complex off-rates in live cells
protocol: Coat glass plates with 100 µL collagen (1:50 in PBS) for 3 hr at 37 °C.
Remove the collagen from the plates.
Plate 4,500-6,000 RPE-1 cells in RPE-1 growth media in each well.
Prepare transfection mixtures by mixing Opti-MEM with Plasmid and Opti-MEM with Lipofectamine separately for 5 min at room temperature.
Incubate the mixed Opti-MEM/Plasmid and Opti-MEM/Lipofectamine solutions together for 30 min at room temperature before use.
Add 80 µL of RPE-1 growth media per well of the transfection mixture.
Remove growth media from cells prepared the previous day.
Add 100 µL of the transfection mixture per well to the cells.
Incubate cells with the transfection mixture for 2-3 hours in a 37°C tissue culture incubator.
Replace the transfection mixture with 100 µL of RPE-1 growth media per well.
Change media by adding 100 µL fresh RPE-1 media per well on Day 3.
Prepare Drug Cocktail I by mixing 247 µL RPE-1 Growth Media and 3 µL 10 mM Y27631.
Prepare Drug Cocktail II by mixing 237 µL RPE-1 Growth Media, 1 µL 10 mM Y27631, 8 µL 1 mM Jasplakinolide, 2 µL 5 mM Latrunculin B, and 2 µL 500 µg/mL nocodazole.
Add 50 µL Drug Cocktail I to one well of a 96-well plate. Incubate for 20 minutes at 37°C.
Add 50 µL Drug Cocktail II to the same well of the 96-well plate. Incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Identify cells to image while incubating with Drug Cocktail II.
Find the plane of the cell in which localization of the nuclear periphery can be observed using a widefield/Yokogawa spinning-disc confocal microscope and 60x water immersion objective.
Use stage controls to find cells that express all constructs of interest.
Observe sufficient expression of the CDK- Δ50 lamin A fluorescent construct for the interacting protein of interest to form a ring of localization.
Note nuclei with Δ50 lamin A expressed can form irregular contours and multi-lobed nuclei, mild cases acceptable.
Image and photobleach cells identified in step 5 within 2 hours after adding drug Cocktail II.
Image cells every second for the first 35 seconds.
Image cells every 5 seconds for the next 90 seconds.
Image cells every 30 seconds until the end of imaging under most conditions.
Photobleach cells after the first five seconds of imaging using an ellipse with widths and heights of 1 µm.
Draw the region of interest (ROI) in Slidebook 6.13 software where photobleaching at the nuclear lamin occurred.
Draw a reference region (REF), a distant nucleoplasmic region within the cell, in Slidebook 6.13 software.
Draw a background (BG) region, an area absent of any cells, in Slidebook 6.13 software.
Export data for the ROI, REF, and BG regions across the imaging time course as an Excel document.
Generate a corrected curve for the fluorescent signal using the equation: CORRECTED CURVE = (ROI-BG)/(REF-BG).
Subtract the first post-photobleaching value from all time points to normalize the corrected curve.
Divide all time points by the average of the pre-photobleaching corrected values to further normalize the corrected curve.
Average the normalized corrected curves of at least 10 cells imaged on at least two separate days.
Plot the standard deviation of the averaged curves.
